item.title: Might be OK as a joke listing, but...
item.content:encoded:
Was this intentionally created as an example of a badly written SCP? It violates at least three rules of design —

  • Super-powered humanoid with no weaknesses (an "X-Man" on steroids)
  • Able to handle notoriously powerful anomalies safely (nothing in the description explains WHY this new skip can handle Shy Guy or the unstoppable lizard)
  • Containment procedure is basically "give the thing whatever it wants or suffer the consequences" (SCP does not stand for "Spoil, Coddle, Pamper"!)

No vote from me; as a serious entry it's trash, as a spoof of bad writers' skips it serves a useful example.

Everyone but the owner of the doll believes that it is creepy, almost horrifyingly so and prefer not to be around it or they will try to get rid of it. The owner on the other hand would believe it gives them some type of protection(I haven't decided if it does or not — maybe it makes them have pleasant dreams and when removed causes nightmares of the doll's "true"/frightening appearance. Testing would be done to see the range of the dolls effects, if they could be used for benefit, how the effects change over distance/if the doll was separated from the owner for a period of time (the discovery on the separation would be that if separated long enough the owner will begin to feel antsy—similar to a withdrawal situation) and also on what exactly the doll/the force behind the doll considers "ownership" (does a previous owner have to die, or is giving the doll up enough?).

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) The First and Forever Prisoner
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Tale

Genre: History

Elevator Pitch: Following the history of the one we know as SCP-682 from it's birth as a child of the Scarlet King, exiled to Earth until she could kill everyone, to being an inmate in Titania's Prison, to trying to release it's father only to be imprisoned by the Keepers. The only thing stopping it from detroying the world has been the legacy of the Jailors that have kept it imprisoned for most of it's existence, the Foundation is only the most recent to inherit the role.

Central Narrative: Connecting the dots between several hints regarding 682
- born as A'zieb, the fourth child/bride of the Scarlet King
- Mal-Va-Gar-Ta-Mor, SCP-2932-A, first imprisonment under the Children of the Night and the Hudaru
- The Bastard Son of Apep, SCP-557-1, the Ancient Containment Site was actually the first version of SCP-2317, the stone in the floor of Room 501 sealing off the Scarlet King(the other door was made later when this way could not be accessed) his fourth child led an army to break his seal only to be imprisoned as well.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This isn't about killing the Hard-to-Kill Reptile, this is about why it matters that it is contained by the Foundation and it's precursors. Also information on why both the Reptile and the King are not meant to be destroyed at all.

Additional Notes: I am also planning on connecting Mekhane/Wan and/or the Lord of Endowments in this story to tie it to another tale I'm working on. The Gods are critical in sealing and containing the Prisoners.

item.content:encoded:

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX, which is not the children but rather what has taken control of the children's consciousness, are interviewed and studied by the researchers. item.title: Re: A Very Sadistic Cap [Seeking Greenlight]
item.content:encoded:
Heyo!

+ show block
– hide block

(any idea how to hide the text? For reason, my brain with two brain-cells can't seem to find the button for it…)

I usually go to this site an copy paste the syntax:

https://www.wikidot.com/doc-wiki-syntax:collapsible-blocks

sorry about all the edits, collapsible texts apparently don't like being formatted:(

Well, I wanted to make the story base on incidents that happened because of the SCP. This was just one of the incidents that the SCP caused.

Incident logs alone won't be able to fully carry the story, as they don't show much of an arc, much less a strong payoff. When pitching the narrative, you're looking to show a brief summary of the whole story, from the setup to the payoff and the main conflict.- its essentially a very brief draft.

The Foundation doesn't catch it because it teleports to different places around the world for another victim, but they are involved and they do learn it has a pattern of where it goes and when it strikes.

This sounds a bit off to me, if it has a pattern then the Foundation should (theoretically) be able to contain it, or at least put more permanent and/or streamlined techniques in place to contain it. Currently their containment method feels fairly makeshift and rough.

This also wasn't mentioned in the narrative pitch much, which makes it hard for me to get an idea of the draft would look like.

I didn't mean to do it in an insensitive way. I wanted to make it creepy and mysterious at the same time.

If you're looking to add mystery, try to allow the story to slowly build anticipation on the questions the concept raised, rather than trying to shoehorn something in quickly.

Hope this cleared some stuff up, let me know if you want any additional feedback :)

Cheers,

RED

item.title: Re: SCP-XXXX - The Division Bell
item.content:encoded:
Hey, thanks for your feedback!

Eh, in my opinion, this feels more like a inspiration of SCP-513 just that the effects of the bell are more violent.

Bugger, I didn't know that one. I wonder now if this has enough to stand on it's own. I am tying it in to historical people and events, and it has different effects, so possibly.

show spoilers
hide spoilers

Honestly, the name came first (after reading Pink Floyd's wikipedia article!). Then thoughts started circulating: a bell that divides people somehow. Option 1: It actually splits them in two somehow, nah, don't like it. Option 2: The sound has an effect on their aggression (stimulates the amygdala? enhanced fight-or-flight reaction?) and causes them to attack other people. From there, I started reading up on the history of bells and how to tie it in to the SCP.
Simultaneously, while I love cool monster SCPs, I also like SCPs where there's a smidge of plausibility. I recently re-read 096 and his rage issues. What if a similar violent rage happened, but to normal people, not a superhuman impossible beastie. We'd be exhausted after a short time and likely to injure ourselves as well as others. Afterwards there would be profound psychological impacts - suicide likely.

How DID they renovate it exactly? You can't leave that blank. While the foundation does leave some stuff away, you have to give a little bit of context.

Well, this is just an ideas critique/greenlight, not a finished draft. But I imagine it's removal of tarnish, re-attachment of the clapper, suspension from a frame, addition of a rope. I might add something if I draft an article, but it's not really important.

I'd recommend you keeping it secret since some SCPs have their locations of where they were found redacted or with a black box. THAT'S what the Foundation does to keep things secret.

Eh, I'm torn on this. The SCP has been removed from the discovery location (and there's nothing anomalous about the location istself). In universe, the SCP data is only available to SCP personnel anyway. I'm not sure what benefit there would be to redacting it, there's not really a reason to keep the location secret. I don't want to redact just for the sake of it.

item.title: SCP-XXXX "The Frozen Wood"
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article, Tale (after SCP is established)

Genre (Optional): Horror, Drama/Emotional

Class: Euclid

Elevator Pitch:

+ show block
– hide block

SCP-XXXX is a snowy, Birch forest varying in size, but often appears in a 10 KM x 12 KM radius. The subject seems to teleport to areas around the world at random (along with anything inside it), leaving a large, empty area in its wake, but is limited to cold climates and/or places that are experiencing severe winter storms. Strangely, the area always seems to be entirely sterile, no life can survive, be it plant, animal, bacteria, or even tardigrade!

Central Narrative:

+ show block
– hide block

The SCP tale I was planning for this follows a lone huntsman as he has unknowingly stumbled into this forest looking for game. He starts feeling weak, his vision blurry, and the snow taking on a slight red-ish hue. He starts coughing up blood, eventually too weak to go any further and contemplates his own mortality as he slowly dies in the snow. A lot of this story will have to do with what goes on in the character's mind, and how he deals with his impending death. (just a summary of the story)

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

+ show block
– hide block

As stated before, the forest cannot support any life whatsoever, except for the trees that grow in it; these trees, designated SCP-XXXX-A, release a toxic, spore-like pollen that sterilizes and kills all known terrestrial lifeforms (many SCP's are not affected), but thankfully, only within it's area of effect. These spores are inhaled and break down the cells of the organism, causing; internal bleeding from torn organ tissue, destruction of muscle fibers/tissue leading to paralysis, vomiting blood, asphyxiation, convulsions and/or seizures, always ending with total organ failure and death.

After tracking it for years and sending hazmat-suit equipped recovery teams into the area, a total of 247 human bodies have been discovered, as well as the corpses of wildlife native to many different regions. Strangely, these bodies were perfectly intact, no decay had occurred as there were no bacteria left to break the bodies down.

Additional Notes:

- The spores from SCP-XXXX-A cannot survive outside of SCP-XXXX's area of effect, thus, the only way to study the spores is to be within the subject itself.

- Due to its often secluded location and it's deadly nature, as long as the Foundation is careful about the spores, a well protected base could be built inside the area as well as utilizing its random teleportation effect to avoid detection by the public!

item.title: Re: A Very Sadistic Cap [Seeking Greenlight]
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for your reply!

+ show block
– hide block

The concept:

Overall, the skip doesn't have much context around it, there's no clear motives and no clear in-universe justification for existing. Which as a result, makes the skip feel close to a "thing that does a thing", along with causing it to just feel like your average murder monster.

I do agree with you that this SCP is basically just a thing that does a thing, but I don't fully agree with the "murder monster" part. It was my fault for not fully explaining it, but the cap doesn't always want to kill people. It just wants to hurt or humiliate its victim the best way it can without killing them.

there's no reason why the skip is a cap, or why the skip specifically has these anomalies (teleportation, telepathy, etc.)

Yeah, I agree with the first part. It being a cap is kinda silly, but how it gets its anomalies was supposed to be a mystery, so it can make it interesting.

or why it's interested in tricking people.

It's not interested in tricking people. It's interested in other peoples' sorrow and will go to great lengths to torment them by making them do terrible stuff to themselves or others for something they will not get in the end. That's why it's called "a very sadistic cap." It enjoys peoples' pain and misery, and that's its motivation to why it does these things.

(EDIT: wait no, I take back. You're right, I don't know why it's interested in tricking people. Maybe I put that in there because I wanted the SCP to be a good manipulator or something.)

The Narrative:

First off, this seems much closer to a single incident rather than a narrative. As there's little to no clear arc, and most questions the concept raised are still left unanswered.

Well, I wanted to make the story base on incidents that happened because of the SCP. This was just one of the incidents that the SCP caused.

Foundation doesn't seem to be involved here at all, there isn't anything showing how they found it, what happened during its containment, and what they learned.

The Foundation doesn't catch it because it teleports to different places around the world for another victim, but they are involved and they do learn it has a pattern of where it goes and when it strikes.

The suicide note feels like a narrative device to drum up tension or make the skip seem more dangerous, which (to me at least) comes off as edgy and a bit cliched, considering how much this sort of storyline is seen in other media.

You're definitely right about this. I was trying to show how manipulative the SCP was and how it's not a thing to mess with, but the suicide note just made it edgy. I kinda cringed a bit when I read it again lol.

on a side note, suicide in general can be a rather sensitive topic, if you do wish to include it, it will need to be handled carefully.

I didn't mean to do it in an insensitive way. I was trying to make the atmosphere creepy and mysterious at the same time by using the paintings, photos, and the suicide note.

Hook:

This if fairly dull, as the skips effects or motives won't be able to carry the article alone, for this to work as a hook (IMO), they would need to be integrated and communicated effectively in the narrative (which currently they aren't). Generally speaking, you're looking to put the main idea or core narrative conflict in the hook.

I agree with this. I will try to change it soon.

Overall, this is some really good critique. Thanks!

item.title: Re: (Seeking Greenlight) The Uncontainable Man
item.content:encoded:
It's just a fact of baseline reality that this anomaly cannot be contained

This might come off as just being overpowered to force the narrative to be what the author wants. It feels more contrived than, say, SCP-1915 (Status Quo) where the anomaly is very difficult to contain, but the reality bending for that anomaly feels inherent to the character's story independent of any authorial meddling.

The overuse of resources and personnel is due to the fact that they can't get him to stay in containment for more than five minutes

My main suspension of disbelief gripe is the Foundation taking so long and using up so many resources before they figure out what they need to do. If you really want to go that route, it's your prerogative as author; however, I would not be greenlighting a premise that relies on that narrative setup.

The character can also be reduced from an arrogant parody of Mary Sues to someone who really, really doesn't want to be locked up.

This approach would be much more workable—fear of being confined is more relatable to the average reader.

Since that time we have expanded to include articles on every aspect of the writing process, fiction, guest posts, blog tours, and more!

item.title: Re: (Seeking Greenlight) The Uncontainable Man
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for the criticism. I still think that this can work, if I change the premise enough:

The "Foundation being incompetent" thing isn't a necessary part of the article, and can be rewritten by making our anomaly a semiohazard, a fact of the universe that shouldn't be true, but is. It's just a fact of baseline reality that this anomaly cannot be contained, just as it is a fact of baseline reality that "The operations of 'YWTGTSYT' are perfectly legal." The overuse of resources and personnel is due to the fact that they can't get him to stay in containment for more than five minutes – and that also applies to the trucks they use to transport him. And while it would make more sense to convince the guy to remain in containment or keep him comatose, the first is not going to happen unless they threaten lethal force (which is what they figure out they have to do) for reasons discussed below, and the second counts as "containment" and thus will not work.

The character can also be reduced from an arrogant parody of Mary Sues to someone who really, really doesn't want to be locked up. He's had nightmares about it, he's always been terrified of it, and getting sentenced to prison confirmed all his worst fears about it. The causal link between this fear and the manifestation of his anomaly is unconfirmed; perhaps this was always a property of him, but it never became an issue until he was carted off to jail. Perhaps he manifested the property after going to jail.

Do you think that could work?

/scp-5127 (The Planet) by GamerboyAli deleted at -17 and three votes.

SCP-5127 is a planet roughly six (6) times bigger than planet Jupiter. SCP-5127's shape is complementary to an oblate spheroid. It appears to look identical to planet Earth. It is believed that one (1) Earth year on SCP-5127 is equal to ten (10) Earth years on Earth. Due to this, SCP-5127's spin speed is roughly 4471 m/s.

Feedback ported:

[+] from JakdragonX
– hide block

Conceptually speaking, this article doesn't really make itself unique. The anomaly just seems to be a bigger, sentient Earth that absorbs planets and materials in order to grow in mass. Theres no further explanation. Nothing for the reader to latch onto or really get involved with. The length doesn't really do it justice in this regard.

Logically, I'm unsure of how researchers would be able to identify that this planet has sentience. Did they go to it and interview it? How do they know that its absorbing mass? There are just a lot of open-ended statements with no real investigation or investment logically to back them up. The suspension of disbelief ultimately broke for me as I read it.

If you decide to rewrite this, I would heavily advocate for expansion. Remove the redactions and the expungments, give us a story, or something more than an empty conceptual trope. Anomalys like this need something to back them up, especially if you're intending to make it short-form. An emotional impact, a conceptually unique or wacky punchline, just anything more than "whoa, neat."

EDIT: Should further mention that including the "O5" in the Containment Procedures just seems like a poor attempt at escalating the "threat" of your anomaly. Theres really no reason behind it, as far as I can tell. Honestly, nothing about the Conprocs actually describe how to contain it at all. Which, is a little weird for me. TL;DR this is just a conceptually boring trope with no story or investment besides it being "cool." You should really try to put a spin on this and include something to attach the readers with, or try a new anomaly (or even expand your wordcount to include addenda and exploration).

[+] from Riemann
– hide block

SCP-5127's shape is complementary to an oblate spheroid.

In mathematics, a complement is the set of elements that complete a universal set that are not part of the set in question, eg, an oblate spheroid.

I know this is a mistake, but this line implies that the shape of 5127 is all R3 embedded shapes that are not an oblate spheroid, which I think is a weirdly fascinating idea.

/scp-5587 (no title) by Gunther Metz summarily deleted at +0 after its author blanked the page. Riemann witnessed.

SCP-5587 appears as a male human child, around ten (10) years of age. Their is no physical oddities about SCP-5587, but he measures in the top 99% in intelligence of all humans. SCP-5587 appears to possess and completely control some form of omnipotence and omnipresence. SCP-5587 is one of the most powerful SCPs, due to his ability to create a XK-class end-of-the-world scenario.

item.title: SCP-XXXX - The Division Bell
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror/History

Elevator Pitch: An archaic bell that when rung instils extreme feelings of revulsion and loathing towards other humans (to the point of violence)

Central Narrative:
Discovery log - This will describe the findings of the archaeological dig where the bell was found. Summarised:
Discovered in the Fens near Crowland Abbey, England.
Surrounded by human skeletal remains bearing signs of violence (broken bones, crushed skulls, incision marks, burn marks, etc.
Dated to circa 710 CE.
Unusual bronze composition (higher than normal tin percentage; presence of antimony - unknown at time bell casting)
Inscription on bell 'belli munus' (Latin for 'gift of war')
Essentially, the discovery log will hint at something unusual, setting the stage for the incident log, where the anomalous properties were discovered.

Incident log - This will describe what happened when a historical society/museum renovated it and rang it for the first time: all attendees consumed with revulsion and/or loathing, leading to much violence including deaths and serious injuries. Probably a description from security and/or news camera footage at the venue.

+ show block
– hide block

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
Addendum 1 - this will link the bell to Guthlac of Crowland - an ascetic hermit monk who later had an abbey built for him by the king of Mercia, and was said to be plagued by demons (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guthlac_of_Crowland). The implication will be that the demons made him create the bell during his isolation.
Addendum 2 - this will briefly describe some lost notes from the Hemony brothers (real world bell founders from the 1600s), with a design identical to the Fens bell - plus documentation that several of these were manufactured and sold (to unknown parties). And possibly notes for an 'improved' design.

Additional Notes:
I'd like to have a sound clip of the bell to either play automatically a certain amount of time after opening the article (creepy but not really within the SCP format) or after clicking one/many links with appropriate warnings/security credentials ('Confirm level 3 access', 'Confirm you are alone', 'Confirm you are shackled' etc.).

item.title: Lost objects appear at 0°N 0°E (Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Anomaly

Page Layout (Optional): Description, table of recovered instances, discovery, addendum with notable events, appendixes with anticipated future events and recommendations.

Elevator Pitch: Objects randomly appear at exactly 0°N 0°E presumably due to teleportation to unset coordinates. The objects intersect with whatever is already there in the ocean in high-energy mergers. Similarly time travel mistakes happen where many objects appear simultaneously at times such the Unix epoch (1970-01-01) and the GPS epoch (1980-01-06) resulting in very large explosions.

Central Narrative: A very large explosion happens at 0°N 0°E on 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC. The Foundation discovers objects randomly appearing there, almost always destroyed by the high-energy intersection with what's already there in the ocean. The objects vary from junk to high tech equipment potentially from the future, accidentally sent to unset coordinates. Further explosions happen during the GPS epochs on 1980-01-01, and 1999-08-21, and the Foundation figures out the computing aspect. The Y2K bug confirms it and the Foundation anticipates further events and mitigates them. It turns out time overflow bugs also caused major explosions back in 1900 and 1901 and more are due in 2036 and 2038. The Foundation recommends switching to better time keeping formats.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Specific containment procedures to stay away from 0°N 0°E (Null Island) with hints of dangerous events that nuclear nations needs to be informed about, a picture of an flaming object manifesting in the ocena.

Additional Notes: I already wrote a complete draft at http://scp-sandbox-3.wikidot.com/sortie but need to go through the greenlight policy as a first time author.

item.title: (Seeking Greenlights and tips!) Portraitly.ai
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror/Sci-Fi

Elevator Pitch:
+Show Elevator Pitch
-Hide Elevator Pitch

An indie neural network project with the purpose of generating human portraits through combining several photographs of different people begins to manifest entities that appear to perfectly match the human shown in the image, except for the absence of any body parts not shown in the image. However, the entities are still able to propel themselves by unknown means. These entities vocalize through a combination of word jumbles composed of both English and French and through EDM bass drop samples. The humanoid entities prove difficult to terminate, as they are able to demanifest their physical form through a crouching motion.

Central Narrative:
+Show Central Narrative
-Hide Central Narrative

SCP-XXXX was first made known to the foundation after a series of reports detailing the sudden manifestation of a disembodied male head outside of the Arvonne Fraser Library in Minneapolis, Minnesota to local authorities. The Minneapolis Police Department passed the reports to the SCP Foundation, which immediately detained the entity and administered amnestics to witnesses of the event as well as propagating an online disinformation campaign, as images of the entity were posted on multiple websites. The entity was then interviewed by the site-19 researcher, Dr. Sharpe. The interview was conducted with the objective of discerning any potential information about the entity that it may be able to convey. Dr. Sharpe ascertained that the entity is capable of simple communication through the use of word association games. During these games, the entity mentions the word "Portraitly" which, after further research into the initial SCP-XXXX event, matched computer browsing history logs from inside the library. The interview was terminated after Dr. Sharpe apparently pointed out a patch of acne under the entity's hairline, which caused the entity to cease cooperation with Dr. Sharpe. The entity is contained in a standard humanoid chamber. Testing of SCP-XXXX determined that Portraitly.ai, a website hosting an anomalous neural network, manifests a seemingly random entity in the area of any subject using the website. Pressing the "Reload" option on Portraitly.ai prompts the website to generate a new image, which in turn manifests a new entity.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
+Show Hook
-Hide Hook

I haven't seen many SCP articles covering neural network sites, so I think it may be interesting to write about one possibly going wrong, especially with the rise of deep fakes and image generators.

Additional Notes: This is my first SCP pitch, so any critique, greenlights, or, advice would be greatly appreciated!

item.title: Re: A Very Sadistic Cap [Seeking Greenlight]
item.content:encoded:
Hello Inertia_comrade! lets take a look :)

SAND

+ show block
– hide block

The concept:

Elevator Pitch: My SCP is a cap that can telepathically talk to their victims and tricks them into believing that it's a higher being, and if they do what it demands, they'll be awarded what they truly wanted in life. When the victim completes their task(s), the SCP disappears and leaves them, so they can suffer for what they have done. (So basically, it's a troll)

Overall, the skip doesn't have much context around it, there's no clear motives and no clear in-universe justification for existing. Which as a result, makes the skip feel close to a "thing that does a thing", along with causing it to just feel like your average murder monster.

Another issue I have with this; everything feels very random and disjointed, there's no reason why the skip is a cap, or why the skip specifically has these anomalies (teleportation, telepathy ect.) or why its interested in tricking people. Currently, there isn't any sort of link between these elements, which as result, causes the concept to feel random and a bit overcomplicated.

The narrative:

Central Narrative: In 2010, a man was found dead in his house from suicide. One of his friends went to check on him and saw that the door was unlocked. He decided to enter the house and noticed there were multiple drawings all over the walls and hundreds of pictures in one of the rooms of the SCP. There was also a message on one of the walls that say this,

"I Don't Understand. I Did Everything It Wanted Me To Do, But I Don't Hear It Anymore. I Made It My God. I Pushed Everyone Away From My Life. I Killed My Own Two Kids For It, And Yet It's Abandons Me. I Guess My Fate Wasn't Good Enough…"

First off, this seems much closer to a single incident rather than a narrative. As there's little to no clear arc, and most questions the concept raised are still left unanswered. Along with this, the Foundation doesn't seem to be involved here at all, there isn't anything showing how they found it, what happened during its containment, and what they learnt.- do note that the article is written from their perspective, they wouldn't be able to write an article without mentioning themselves, or what they ended up doing.

As for the narrative itself, it feels like your average murder monster horror story, there's nothing here that really stands out or makes the narrative interesting. The suicide note feels like a narrative device to drum up tension or make the skip seem more dangerous, which (to me at least) comes off as edgy and a bit cliched, considering how much this sort storyline is seen in other media.- on a side note, suicide in general can be a rather sensitive topic, if you do wish to include it, it will need to handled carefully.

Hook:

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The cap can somehow teleport to different places in the world, causing more harm to others. The cap does these things to people because it finds it entertaining.

This if fairly dull, as the skips effects or motives won't be able to carry the article alone, for this to work as a hook (imo), they would need to be integrated and communicated effectively in the narrative (which currently they aren't). Generally speaking, you're looking to put the main idea or core narrative conflict in the hook.

Red or green?
Due to my afore mentioned concerns, no-greenlight.

My recommendations;

- Link all of the concept main elements with each-other, try not to use "somehow" to describe why it has its effects, as it makes the concept feel unfinished/anticlimactic.

-Give the skip a strong motive, show why its like this, and how its end goals/motives affect the narrative.- generally speaking, if you know what the skips end goal is, is much easier to craft a storyline.

- Create a stronger storyline, show more of an arc. Here are some questions you can try building off - how does the Foundation deal with the skip? what do they end up learning? whats the main conflict? who are the characters? how will those characters make me feel? how would I feel by the end of the narrative? whats the main payoff?-what is the narrative building up to?

If you would like me review this (or any concept) further, then please feel free to send me a PM or ask via IRC. Response times generally range from 2-12 hours over PMs. If your looking for additional critiques in general, then I would highly recommend contacting the butterfly squad :)

Cheers,

-RED

item.title: Re: Star Euthanizer
item.content:encoded:
{Placeholder}

On to the critique ->
– hide block

SPaG

On 28 August 1903, Foundation personnel educated in astrology sighted SCP-XXXX through a telescope near the Orion Arm.

This suggests that the telescope was situated in the Orion's Arm spiral arm, rather than the object was located in that sector. Additionally, "astrology" is defined by Merriam-Webster as "the divination of the supposed influences of the stars and planets on human affairs and terrestrial events by their positions and aspects". I believe the word you are looking for is "astronomy".

"sighted" is also defined as "able to see : not blind." Perhaps "observed".

Consistency/Flow

All deep-space observatories are to be monitored by satellite following standard procedure.

This could be cleaned up a bit to be more specific. It is unclear which standard procedure is being followed. Furthermore, I would assume that all deep space observations would be closely monitored by the SCPF as a matter of course.

The production and trade of new telescope parts such as refractors have been limited to companies where a sufficient number of undercover Foundation personnel are present.

This is also jumbled and unclear. What is this meant to prevent?

All images of SCP-XXXX are to be intercepted by the Foundation AI "Binary star", saved in the Foundation database, and subsequently deleted from public records.

I have a personal preference for utilizing the .aic convention. In this case, your AI would become Binary_Star.aic. I think it looks cleaner than "name", in that it specifies an entity rather than a "supposed" entity. It's all in the implication.

SCP-XXXX is the first spacecraft ever observed by the Foundation.

Non-human or non-terrestrial? Or did this observation predate Sputnik and the other Earth-based spacecraft?

Closing Remarks

There are significant errors throughout this piece, what is represented here are just a few examples. The idea is a sound one and I think the additional story told throughout the listpages is interesting. However, there are a lot of sentence structure and word choice errors that make this difficult to read.

Ping me on IRC at your leisure and we can go over more of them if you'd like.
